overall_design: HepG2 WT and FoxO1-KO cells were cultured in Dulbecco's modified Eagle's medium supplemented with 10% fetal bovine serum and 1% antibiotic . The cells were collected for transcriptome sequencing after treatment with 1μg/mL LPS for 24 h.
summary: The transcription factor Forkhead box protein O1 (FoxO1) is a well-established regulator of glucose and lipid metabolism, yet its role in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) pathogenesis remains debated. This study investigates hepatocyte-specific FoxO1 mechanisms driving hepatic inflammation in MASH. Using hepatocyte-specific FoxO1-knockout (KO) mice fed a methionine-choline-deficient diet and LPS-treated FoxO1-KO cells, we demonstrate FoxO1 depletion exacerbates hepatic inflammation, ballooning degeneration, and upregulates TNF-alpha, CXCL8, and CXCL2 in vivo and in vitro. Transcriptomics linked FoxO1 deficiency to enriched pro-inflammatory pathways and suppressed cysteine/methionine metabolism.
title: Hepatocyte FoxO1 depletion exacerbates hepatic inflammation in MASH
type: Expression profiling by high throughput sequencing
